records.central_claim: Ulama de cadera is a living Sinaloan form of the Mesoamerican rubber-ball tradition. It is played with a heavy solid rubber ball struck with the hip (sources also describe the upper thigh) and protective gear; Mexican and scholarly sources characterize it as a survival of, or closely related to, the pre-Hispanic ballgame. Archaeology supports a Mesoamerican ballgame by about 1650 BCE, but does not establish that modern ulama’s rules have remained unchanged or continuously documented for 3,400 years, nor that it is definitively the world’s oldest team sport.
